author: opencode-worker-6
text: Worker-6 seam survey (released at timebox; no code landed). Concrete implementation plan for the Rust wiring: (1) DATA-PATH: the egress decap happens in lichen-node receive.rs:292-300 (ingest_border_frame's EGRESS DECapsulation branch, R-05-063) — extend that branch to carry the consumed SRH route hops out with the outcome (add a route-evidence field to RplBorderIngressOutcome::Ipv6, e.g. Option<Vec<[u8;8]>>, sourced from the survey's SourceRouted view before decapsulate_ipv6 consumes the outer; keep the shared RplReceiveOutcome untouched to avoid churning every match site). (2) GATEWAY GATE: in Gateway::ingest_mesh_frame_at_superframe (gateway.rs:1306) where DeliveredIpv6 maps to upstream_ipv6, construct tunnel_auth::DecapsulationRequest { direction: MeshToExternal, route: <evidence>, inner_source, destination_is_mesh: false, source_is_mesh: true } and call TunnelAuthorizationTable::authorize_decapsulation(&mut table, request, now_ms) before setting upstream_ipv6; unauthorized -> warn + drop (None). The gateway struct needs a TunnelAuthorizationTable field + set_root(root_iid) at provisioning; table capacity DEFAULT_AUTHORIZATION_CAPACITY. (3) POST ENDPOINT BLOCKER: lichend.rs has NO CoAP server at all (grep coap = only GatewayCoordinator resource structs) — mounting POST /.well-known/tunnel-auth requires a CoAP server decision for lichend (which stack: aiocoap-equivalent? lichen-coap rust crate server?) — flagged back to the parent as a prerequisite decision. (4) Tests: extend tunnel_auth_vectors.rs with the wired-path cases (authorized tunnel forwarded, unauthorized dropped, expired dropped, wrong-direction rejected) using the existing ingest fixture + a stub table entry via accept_post with AuthenticatedRoot.
